---
title: "PROC SORT and PROC TRANSPOSE"
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

```{r setup}
library(sasonr)
```

PROC SORT and PROC TRANSPOSE reshape data sets; they write no listing, only
the data set and the NOTEs of the log.

```{r}
prog <- "
data labs;
  input subj $ visit param $ aval;
  datalines;
S02 1 ALT 31
S01 2 ALT 28
S01 1 ALT 25
S02 2 ALT .
S01 1 AST 22
S02 1 AST 30
;
run;
"
```

## PROC SORT

`BY` sorts in ascending order; `DESCENDING` reverses the variable after it.
Missing values sort before every number. `OUT=` writes a new data set and
leaves the input as it is.

```{r}
res <- sas_run(paste(prog, "
proc sort data=labs out=bysubj;
  by subj descending visit;
run;"))
res$work$bysubj
cat(sas_log(res), sep = "\n")
```

`NODUPKEY` keeps the first observation of each BY group and writes how many
it deleted.

```{r}
res <- sas_run(paste(prog, "
proc sort data=labs out=first nodupkey;
  by subj;
run;"))
res$work$first
```

### As an R call

The translation of a PROC SORT step is one call of `sas_proc_sort()`, the
call `sas_run()` itself runs: `data` and `out` name the data sets, `by` takes
variable names with `desc()` for a descending one (or the BY text as
strings), switches such as `nodupkey` are `TRUE`.

```{r}
res <- sas_run(paste(prog, "proc sort data=labs out=bysubj; by subj descending visit; run;"))
cat(tail(as.character(sas_script(res)), 3), sep = "\n")
```

```{r}
s <- sas_session()
invisible(sas_run(prog, session = s))
s |> sas_proc_sort(data = "labs", out = "first", by = subj, nodupkey = TRUE)
sas_work(s)$first
```

### On a data frame

`sas_sort_df()` sorts a data frame the same way without a session.

```{r}
df <- data.frame(subj = c("S02", "S01", "S01"), aval = c(31, NA, 25))
sas_sort_df(df, by = c("subj", "aval"))
```

## PROC TRANSPOSE

`ID` names the new columns, `BY` keeps one row per group, `VAR` chooses the
variables to transpose; `_NAME_` holds the name of the transposed variable.

```{r}
res <- sas_run(paste(prog, "
proc sort data=labs; by subj visit; run;
proc transpose data=labs out=wide;
  by subj visit;
  id param;
  var aval;
run;"))
res$work$wide
```

### As an R call

`sas_proc_transpose()` is the call of the translation; options are arguments
(`out = "wide"`, `prefix = "v_"`), statements are variable names.

```{r}
cat(tail(as.character(sas_script(res)), 3), sep = "\n")
```

```{r}
s <- sas_session()
invisible(sas_run(paste(prog, "proc sort data=labs; by subj visit; run;"), session = s))
s |> sas_proc_transpose(data = "labs", out = "wide", prefix = "v_", by = c(subj, visit), var = aval)
sas_work(s)$wide
```

### On a data frame

`sas_transpose_df()` takes the same arguments with a data frame.

```{r}
df <- data.frame(subj = c("S01", "S01", "S02"), param = c("ALT", "AST", "ALT"), aval = c(25, 22, 31))
sas_transpose_df(df, var = aval, by = subj, id = param)
```
